notes: This aggregation combines completed reports. public-library and library-rust were rerun for the public Data.Function.Sub.Aff.Do addition. The seven other native suites retain their earlier completed runs and are not represented as fresh reruns.

public-library has 56 typing cases and one JavaScript execution, including the new 12-assertion Aff.Do protocol test. After the complete rerun, AffDoDuplicateResource was refined to isolate bind from pure and rechecked independently with the expected NoInstanceFound diagnostic in bind. The targeted rerun is recorded in that suite.
The standard Spago test path also passed with --offline --strict: zero warnings and zero errors. refs was added explicitly to test dependencies and the lockfile was regenerated by Spago.

library-rust has five typing cases and three executions: public pure tests in normal and threaded modes, and the unchanged public Aff.Do runtime test in threaded mode. Its source fingerprints match the current files.

The totals count 135 PureScript typing cases and 19 successful program executions: one JavaScript and 18 Rust. Standalone rustc controls and external b8x application runs are retained separately and excluded from those totals.
The earlier normal-mode Aff port build rejection remains recorded separately and is not counted as a successful execution. The new Aff.Do runtime test was executed on Rust in threaded mode only.

Other package Rust suites use separate experimental APIs. Their borrowing, lifetime and thread-affinity features are not automatically features of the public library. The b8x production integrations were not changed or rerun for this library addition.
Explicit unsafe controls are typechecked only and are never executed. Accepted ordinary aliases, replayed actions and escaped effects are not automatically safety guarantees.

sourceSha256 is the current source/configuration snapshot; historical runs have not been relabelled. Compiler fingerprints identify the binaries used for the refreshed suites. Machine-specific compiler paths are omitted.

Aff.Do sequences resource transitions and restricts callback results to Shared. Trusted primitives and Shared instances remain part of the contract; exception/cancellation cleanup belongs to the resource runner, not the generic bind.
